title: Freya and the Debt
premise: Beatrix Okafor, a whistle-blower living under four names, works cases no one wants attributed — until the safe house he's hidden in for three years is listed for sale online, with photos of the inside, down to the taped-over smoke detector where he hides his drives. The listing is a message from Halcyon Group, the black-ops training program that made him and now hunts its leakers. With the help of Freya Lindqvist, the estate agent whose face he can't stop remembering from a night he was trained to forget, Beatrix has seventy-two hours before the border checkpoint shifts change to burn Halcyon's network from the inside. He succeeds at the cost of his fourth and truest name, choosing at last to belong to a person rather than a purpose.
about_author: Odile Dravenmoor is the pseudonym of a former intelligence analyst who writes thrillers from a coastal town she refuses to name. Her novels are known for their cold procedural precision and their stubborn, aching faith in love.

chapters.title: The House That Photographed Itself
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Scrolling listings at 3 a.m., he finds the safe house for sale, every room photographed, including the detector hiding his drives. Panic and fury: someone inside his protection detail is selling him. Emotional beat: the floor of a paranoid life gives way.

chapters.title: Four Names, None Mine
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with flashback. He inventories his identities — passports, habits, dead men's birthdays — and realizes the listing used his third name's spelling. Emotional beat: grief for the self he no longer owns.

chapters.title: Freya at the Door
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The estate agent arrives to 'show' the property, and Beatrix recognizes her from a Halcyon training op in Malmö he was drugged through. She claims not to know him. Emotional beat: recognition as a wound reopening.

chapters.title: The Listing Agent
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She admits she was hired anonymously, paid in untraceable crypto, told to photograph everything. She shows him the brief — and his own face, younger, labeled ASSET 7. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He decodes the listing's metadata: a countdown. Halcyon will relocate its archive before the border checkpoint shift change, after which his testimony dies. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Detector Kept
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She helps him retrieve the drives, and he confesses what Halcyon trained him to do — and what he refused to do. Emotional beat: intimacy through confession.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers to Anything
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A former handler, Voss, contacts him with an offer: surrender the drives, live under a fifth name. Beatrix hears the trap in the kindness. Emotional beat: temptation and contempt.

chapters.title: Malmö, Again
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They travel to her hometown to find the trainer who wiped Beatrix's memory of her. He finds a fragment: her voice reading him a poem through a wall. Emotional beat: love as recovered evidence.

chapters.title: Asset 7's Handler
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The old trainer, dying and afraid, gives up the archive's location — a decommissioned customs depot at the border. Emotional beat: pity for the machinery that made him.

chapters.title: The Shift Change
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They map the checkpoint rotations and discover the window is forty minutes, not seventy-two hours. Halcyon moved it up. Emotional beat: the clock collapsing.

chapters.title: Someone Sold the Inside
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He identifies the leak — his own protection officer, whose daughter Halcyon holds. Instead of exposing him, Beatrix recruits him. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy.

chapters.title: Freya's Fourth Wall
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She reveals she took the listing job deliberately, hunting Halcyon for erasing her sister, another Asset. The alliance becomes a vow. Emotional beat: two griefs locking together.

chapters.title: The Depot
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Recon of the customs depot: biometric locks, a server hall, and Voss waiting in plain sight, expecting him. Emotional beat: the hunter's calm before the hunt inverts.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Voss offers Beatrix reinstatement, memory restoration, a self returned. Freya watches him almost take it. Emotional beat: love against duty at its sharpest edge.

chapters.title: The Burn
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He enters the depot under Voss's terms and begins seeding the archive with a dead-man's-switch exfiltration. Emotional beat: cold, methodical courage.

chapters.title: Checkpoint North
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The exfiltration triggers early; alarms; the forty-minute window begins. She drives the escape route while he runs the servers. Emotional beat: terror in tandem.

chapters.title: What Halcyon Trained Me For
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Cornered, he uses his training against his trainers — turning their own protocols, their own certainty, into the weapon. Emotional beat: the made thing unmaking its makers.

chapters.title: The Archive Burns
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The servers die; the drives sync out; Voss is arrested by the very inspectors Halcyon owned, now unowned. Emotional beat: catharsis, disbelieving.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Offered a new identity abroad, Beatrix declines. He surrenders the four names and gives a statement under his own. Emotional beat: belonging chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The hearings begin; Halcyon's network unravels publicly. Freya's sister's file surfaces, and Freya finally mourns. Emotional beat: grief with a floor beneath it.

chapters.title: The House, Sold
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The safe house sells to a young family. Beatrix and Freya watch the movers carry out his old life. Emotional beat: lightness after years of weight.

chapters.title: Freya and the Debt
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, brief. On her coast, Beatrix — nameless by choice, known to one person — pays back the debt he owes her: the memory she returned, returned as a future. Final beat: love against duty, love winning.
